title: Abduction by implicit hitting sets (AbHS)
description: Cost-optimal abduction with an implicit hitting set loop in the style of AbHS (Saikko, Wallner and Järvisalo): the abstraction proposes a cheapest set of hypotheses (A.solve(optimal)); one check looks for a witness that the set is consistent with the theory (no witness: its minimal unsat core must be hit), a second one for a counterexample to the entailment of the manifestations (a model refutes every set it makes true: one of the hypotheses false in it must be added). The first set that passes both checks is a cheapest explanation; track draws the lower bound.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The theory, the hypotheses and the manifestations. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
clause(C) :- pos(C,_).
clause(C) :- neg(C,_).
atom(A) :- pos(_,A).
atom(A) :- neg(_,A).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): any set of at most k hypotheses.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: any set of hypotheses, cheapest first (each hypothesis costs 1, or cost(H,C)).
{ assume(H) : hypothesis(H) }.
price(H,C) :- hypothesis(H), cost(H,C).
price(H,1) :- hypothesis(H), not cost(H,_).
#minimize { C,H : assume(H), price(H,C) }.
#show assume/1.
% 'always' is true in every candidate. The check blames it when a counterexample does
% not depend on the candidate: then no candidate is a solution.
{ always }.
:- not always.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the assumed hypotheses.

fragments.name: consistent
fragments.description: The first check (solver C1): a witness that theory and hypotheses are consistent.
fragments.text:
% A witness, not a counterexample: a model of the theory in which the assumed
% hypotheses hold. If there is none, the hypotheses contradict the theory, and the
% unsat core names the hypotheses that are to blame.
{ w(A) } :- atom(A).
:- clause(C), not w(A) : pos(C,A); w(A) : neg(C,A).
:- assume(H), not w(H).
#show w/1.

fragments.name: entails
fragments.description: The second check (solver C2): a model in which a manifestation is false.
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a model of the theory and the assumed hypotheses in which some
% manifestation is false. Then the hypotheses do not entail the manifestations.
{ m(A) } :- atom(A).
:- clause(C), not m(A) : pos(C,A); m(A) : neg(C,A).
:- assume(H), not m(H).
:- m(A) : manifestation(A).
#show m/1.

% The model refutes every set of hypotheses that are all true in it. So a hypothesis
% that is false in the model has to be assumed.
relevant(assume(H)) :- hypothesis(H), not m(H).
% If all hypotheses are true in the model, nothing explains the manifestations: blame
% the atom that is always true.
missing :- hypothesis(H), not m(H).
relevant(always) :- not missing.

loop.text:
solver A  = shared + abstraction
solver C1 = shared + consistent
solver C2 = shared + entails       options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G1 = A -> C1 via shared + glue
link   G2 = A -> C2 via shared + glue

# Implicit hitting sets for abduction (AbHS): the cheapest hypothesis set that hits every
# lesson so far. Inconsistent: its minimal core must be hit (drop one of these). Not
# entailing: a model in which a manifestation is false refutes every set that is true in
# it (add one of the hypotheses false there). The first set that passes both is optimal.
loop:
    M = A.solve(optimal)
    if not M: stop "no explanation"
    track lower = M.cost
    if not C1.solve(assume G1(M)):
        A.add(C1.core.minimal.on(G1))
    else:
        X = C2.solve(assume G2(M))
        if X:
            A.add(G2.clause(M, X))
        else:
            log "a cheapest explanation, cost", M.cost
            accept M
            stop

library.summary: Cost-optimal abduction by implicit hitting sets (AbHS): a cheapest hypothesis set, refined by minimal cores of a consistency witness and by counterexamples to the entailment.

instances.facts:
% Why does the car not start? A theory in clause form:
% pos(C,A): atom A occurs in clause C, neg(C,A): its negation does.
neg(1,flat).    pos(1,nostart).                   % a flat battery: no start
neg(2,flat).    pos(2,dim).                       % a flat battery: dim lights
neg(3,empty).   pos(3,nostart).                   % an empty tank: no start
neg(4,starter). pos(4,nostart).                   % a broken starter: no start
neg(5,plugs).   neg(5,damp). pos(5,nostart).      % fouled plugs in a damp engine: no start
neg(6,cold).    pos(6,flat). pos(6,damp).         % a cold night: flat battery or damp engine
neg(7,lights).  pos(7,flat).                      % lights left on: flat battery
neg(8,rain).    pos(8,damp).                      % rain: damp engine
pos(9,gauge).                                     % the fuel gauge shows fuel
neg(10,gauge).  neg(10,empty).                    % ... so the tank is not empty
% What may be assumed, and what has to be explained.
hypothesis(flat; empty; starter; plugs; cold; lights; rain).
manifestation(nostart).

% A patient with fever and a cough; which diseases explain both?
neg(1,flu).       pos(1,fever).                   % flu: fever
neg(2,flu).       pos(2,cough).                   % flu: cough
neg(3,cold).      pos(3,cough).                   % a cold: cough
neg(4,infection). pos(4,fever).                   % an infection: fever
neg(5,allergy).   pos(5,cough).                   % an allergy: cough
neg(6,allergy).   neg(6,infection).               % (the allergy test rules out an infection)
neg(7,covid).     pos(7,fever). pos(7,cough).     % covid: fever and cough
pos(8,vaccinated).                                % the patient is vaccinated ...
neg(9,vaccinated). neg(9,covid).                  % ... so it is not covid
hypothesis(flu; cold; infection; allergy; covid).
manifestation(fever; cough).

% The only hypothesis that would explain the symptom contradicts the theory.
neg(1,leak).  pos(1,wet).                         % a leak: a wet floor
pos(2,dry).                                       % the pipes are dry ...
neg(3,dry).   neg(3,leak).                        % ... so there is no leak
neg(4,spill). pos(4,sticky).                      % a spill: a sticky floor
hypothesis(leak; spill).
manifestation(wet).
